lens_summary: DIVISIONS. Short answer: no path moves public div_J by >= +0.2 by 29 Sep. Arithmetic (own python; public TP/FP/FN are GUESSES consistent with J_pub 0.36 from probe 26, exp45 = 0.911): with D = TP+FP+FN of 25-50, +0.2 J means recovering 45% of the public FN (10/22, 8/17 or 5/11) with ZERO extra FP. Our best confirmed insertion (DaughterNet v1 + steal) recovered 4/71 FN (5.6%) and added 11 FP on CONFIRMATION (CONTEXT.md 2026-09-24 00:40). That is about 8x short on recall at worse precision. The lab reach audits bound it too: parent + both daughters are detected for 136/151 GT divisions under the window rule, but only 58/151 are orphan-reachable (B32/B35 A0, CONTEXT.md 2026-09-22/24). Only about 3% of insertions land on annotated cells at all (research/wf_ideas_v2/r1_research_div-cap-private-j.json). Each public event is worth a lot: -1 FP fork = +0.007..0.015 J (+0.0007..0.0015 score); an added evaluable fork is worth +0.006..0.013 J at precision 0.5 and ~0 at precision 0.27. So the division term moves in steps of 1-3 events, which is below the LB noise of ~0.003. Top teams probably do NOT win on divisions: a forum report puts divJ ~0.28 at adj 0.89 (Lime1123, research/browser_research_2026-09-24.md l.100), and 0.969-0.975 is only reachable with adj_edge ~0.93-0.94 (inference). Their division gain would come from retrained detectors: dividing nuclei shrink, and the detector misses one daughter in about a fifth of divisions. Realistic ceiling of this lens by 29 Sep: +0.002..+0.005 public score (div_J +0.02..0.05) if everything goes right. Expected: +0.001..+0.002, most of it already in probe 35. Metric facts that matter (tools/official/src/tracking_cellmot/division_metrics.py): the fork may sit at t-1..t+1 of the GT divider; a daughter lineage = child + its successors; FP = considered-but-not-TP + evaluable (the parent matches an annotated non-terminal GT node) + cross-component (children match two different GT tracks) + malformed (a child with in-degree > 1). Forks among unannotated cells are free. One error in an old test: the ILP division weight probe (probe 3, 1.2 -> 0.9) could not change output forks. The motion relink rebuilds edges one-to-one before safe-div (discussions_summary.md l.318), and the ILP emits 0 forks in 1.46M solution edges (CONTEXT.md). So 'let the linker make divisions' was never tested. Re-solving the ILP is too costly now. Idea 2 uses the edge network's pairwise evidence post hoc instead. x138 already exposes the inputs these ideas need, as unused knobs: a candidate-edge dump (BIOHUB_CACHE_EDGE_THRESHOLD, set to 1.0 = off) and a sub-threshold peak dump (LOWDET 0.3 -> low_coords/low_score in the edge_cache npz) (experiments/ext_x138/biohub-x138.ipynb cells 0 and 4). x138 has NO DivNet veto, and its safe divisions are parent <= 9, sister <= 14, mutual NN, divergence 2.25, symmetry 0.6, DeepCenter 0.25 (cell 5).

challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: Probe 3 could not have changed the output forks. The ILP returns 0 forks at weight 1.2, and the motion relink (flow relink on x138) rebuilds all edges one-to-one before safe divisions, which destroys any ILP fork. So 'the linker's own division evidence' has never reached the submission. The closure holds for re-solving with a lower weight, but not for using the edge network's pairwise probability of the second daughter edge.

Those settings were chosen on exp39 tails. On x138 the pool differs: readmitted real peaks become orphan starts, the gap filler adds nodes, the flow relink uses a 7 um gate, and head-refined coordinates move nodes 0.74 um on average. Two structural leaks also remain. (a) Insertion runs post-tail, so second daughters whose orphan track was shorter than MIN_TRACK_LEN 6 were already deleted: 10 local GT divisions lose their daughter node between ckpt and final (r1_hyp_divisions.json insert-at-ckpt). (b) Gap-synthetic nodes are excluded as v, but readmit/gapfill nodes on x138 are not flagged, and their edge_prob is 0.0, so they are steal-eligible by default. A lab on x138 tails lets us set cap/threshold/steal/geometry for the pool we actually ship, and test a second insertion slot right after safe divisions (before the short-track filter) so that inserted daughter tracks are protected as division components.

hypotheses.title: Score second-daughter candidates with the edge network's own p(u->v) from x138's candidate-edge dump
hypotheses.mechanism: Every fork in our output comes from post-hoc geometry (safe-div) or DaughterNet (node-level p_par x p_dau). Neither says whether v is u's daughter, as opposed to a neighbour's. This is exactly the within-parent ambiguity that sank B20 (DivNet 'one p per parent' -> 319 FP). The SimpleNodeTransformer scores every candidate pair (u, v) within the candidate radius with image + neighbourhood context, and it was trained on GT edges that include both daughter edges. Its evidence never reaches the output: the ILP's division weight 1.2 prevents forks, and the one-to-one relink would erase them anyway (see challenged_assumptions). x138 already has a switch that dumps candidate edges with their probability (BIOHUB_CACHE_EDGE_THRESHOLD, currently 1.0 = off). With the dump on, the insertion score becomes p_par(u) x p_dau(v) x p_dau(c1)^a x p_edge(u,v)^b. A second-daughter candidate then needs node-level mitosis evidence AND pairwise-link evidence. This resolves which v, which is the precision lever the linajea cell-state work shows (FP divisions 0.89 -> 0.11 when parent->daughter consistency constrains the solver).
hypotheses.change: Kernel (--base x138): set BIOHUB_CACHE_EDGE_THRESHOLD=0.05 so the predictor writes candidate edges >= 0.05 per movie (edge_cache npz). In the tail, load them into a dict {(u,v): p}, mapping pre-ILP candidate ids to final node ids. Readmit/gapfill nodes have no candidate edges -> p_edge = 0 -> never inserted by this branch. In tools/div_insert.py add params beta (default 0 = exact no-op) and p_edge_min. Score = current score x p_edge(u,v)^beta, and require p_edge(u,v) >= p_edge_min when beta > 0. Optionally a steal branch requires p_edge(u,v) > p_edge(w,v) + margin (replaces the steal_prob_max rule, which today steals from any unscored 0.0 edge). Lab: build the x138 cache of idea 1 with the dump on and grid beta {0,0.5,1}, p_edge_min {0,0.2,0.4}.

hypotheses.title: Recover missing second daughters from x138's sub-threshold peak dump at the mirror position
hypotheses.mechanism: The detector misses one daughter in about a fifth of divisions because dividing nuclei shrink (half-max volume -0.17..-0.27 at +1..+3 frames). Parent + both daughters are detected for only 121-123/151 direct (136/151 under the window rule). A full-frame threshold-0.90 pass reaches 151/151 but at +24% nodes, which was closed on node budget. x138 already computes the needed side table: the LOWDET dump stores every peak >= 0.3 with its sigmoid score (int16 coords), and readmit/gapfill use only peaks within 4 um of open track ends/starts. A capped, targeted lookup costs ~0 nodes: only around high-p_par parents whose single child c1 has no admissible orphan sister, search the dump at t+1 near the mirror point 2u - c1.
hypotheses.change: New branch 'mirror' in tools/div_insert.py (default off). For u with out-degree 1 (child c1 at t+1) and no orphan/steal triple, take the low peaks x at t+1 with score >= h_min (0.5/0.7/0.9), not within 2 um of an existing node, sister(c1,x) in [6, 14.5] um, |u-x| <= 11 um, cos(c1-u, x-u) <= 0.25, and |x - (2u - c1)| <= 5 um. Score = p_par(u) x p_dau(c1)^a x h(x) x exp(-|x - mirror|^2 / 2s^2). Add node x (flag mirror_synthetic) and edge u->x. If a free orphan start or low peak lies within 4 um at t+2, also add x->that (so the metric's grandchild fallback and the short-track filter are satisfied). Cap 1-2 per video. p_par for these u is needed: score them in the same DaughterNet pass (adds ~a few hundred crops per video, guess).

hypotheses.title: Model-free FP-fork removal on x138 safe-division forks (midpoint/angle), bundled with the insertion
hypotheses.mechanism: With J_pub ~0.36, removing one evaluable FP fork is worth +0.007..0.015 J, i.e. about as much as a new TP at precision 0.5, and it cannot hurt edges much. Our FP forks are 'continuation + neighbour on the same side': the parent is not between the two children. Locally all 23 TP forks have mid = |P - (c1+c2)/2| <= 3.76 um and cos(c1-P, c2-P) <= 0.00, while 11-14 of 43 FP forks exceed mid 4.0 or cos 0.1. x138's safe-division gates check parent/sister radii, divergence and symmetry, but not midpoint or angle. The rule uses only geometry, which transfers (unlike rules that trust network confidence).
hypotheses.change: Last graph edit before writing (after divinsert): for every fork created by safe divisions (edge_prob None & safe_division=1), un-fork when mid >= 4.5 um OR cos >= 0.1. Drop the ILP-side edge when its edge_prob is 0.0 (unscored relink), else drop the added edge. Never touch nodes or DaughterNet-inserted forks (their TP mids reach 5.9 um). New patch --patch forkmid for --base x138 with FORKMID_ENABLE (0 = byte-identical).
